docs.task: How execution costs are recorded and summed into a session's cost, and how executions map to stages.

asks: Explain how execution costs are recorded.
Explain how they are summed into a session's cost.
Explain how executions map to stages.

data_flow.step: The planner decides a spawn. `Planner::spawn` computes `stage_of(&purpose)` and stores it in the `SpawnRequest`. Consult spawns set `stage: rec.stage` from the asking run instead.

The runner (after getting a slot and passing the budget check in the planner) appends `ExecutionStarted { stage: req.stage, ... }` to the event log, then inserts the `executions` row with `stage: Some(req.stage)`, `usage` default, `cost_usd` 0. A resumed (paused) execution appends `ExecutionResumed` instead, reopens the row, and takes its stored usage as `usage_base`.
The fold records the run: `ExecutionStarted` inserts an `ExecRecord` with `stage` and `result: None`. `ExecutionResumed` clears `result`.

While the executor runs it sends `ExecutionDelta::Usage` to `EngineHost::emit`. The host adds the delta to `usage_base`, writes the cumulative usage and `cost_usd` column with `update_execution_usage` (`Executions::set_usage`), and recomputes the session's cost as the sum of `cost_usd` over `list_executions(session)` plus the in-memory judge tally, writing it to `sessions.cost_usd` and broadcasting `SessionUpdated`. Running executions are therefore counted here.
Judge calls (not executions) add their `usage.cost_usd` to `Inner::judge_cost[session]` after each successful call. No row, no event carries it.

When the executor returns, `result.usage = usage_base + result.usage`, `finish_execution` writes status, usage, and `cost_usd`, and `ExecutionFinished { id, result }` is appended. The fold sets `ExecRecord.result`.

`Inner::append` runs for every event: stores, materializes, folds, then calls `view::summary(&st, ws, judge_cost)` for the other fields and overwrites `cost_usd` with `list_executions(session)` sum plus judge cost (falling back to the summary value on a DB error).

Reads: `view::detail` loads `db.list_executions`, builds `summary(s, ws, 0.0)` (finished executions from the fold, no judge cost) and sets `summary.cost_usd = max(that, sum of DB execution costs)`. `view::tree_session` does the same with `max(summary.cost_usd, spent)`. `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/cost` runs `Costs::report` across all sessions.
Budget: the planner calls `SessionState::spent_usd()` (finished executions only, from the fold, no judge cost) and opens `GatePayload::BudgetReached` when it is at least `budget + budget_raised`.

patterns.description: An execution's Usage is a running total. A resumed execution (Rule P2) starts from the stored usage of its earlier part (usage_base). EngineHost::emit adds each executor delta to usage_base, stores it, and recomputes the session cost. After the executor returns, the result's usage is usage_base plus the run's usage, so the last ExecutionFinished already includes earlier parts and must not be summed with them.
patterns.name: Usage accumulation with usage_base

patterns.description: (1) `EngineHost::emit` (runner.rs:3008): sum of `executions.cost_usd` over `list_executions(session)` (includes running executions) plus `judge_cost`. (2) `Inner::append` (runner.rs:1419): the same sum plus `judge_cost`, on every event; falls back to `view::summary` when the DB read fails. (3) `view::summary` (view.rs:24): fold-side sum of finished executions' `result.usage.cost_usd` plus the judge cost passed in; `view::detail` passes 0.0 and then takes `max(summary, DB sum)` (view.rs:1194-1196); `view::tree_session` takes `max(summary.cost_usd, spent)` (view.rs:1068). (4) `SessionState::spent_usd` (state.rs:1343): finished executions only, no judge cost, used only by the budget guard in plan.rs. `judge_cost` is `Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, f64>>` on `Inner`, incremented at runner.rs:1984, never written to the log or a table, and not reseeded in `recover` or `load` (grep finds only the uses listed in the files entry). So judge cost is lost on a server restart, and `sessions.cost_usd` drops by it at the next refresh. Judge spend belongs to no execution row and has no stage. Executions with `session_id` NULL (side-panel quick answers at runner.rs:2824 and inspect runs at runner.rs:962) both insert `stage: None`, so they appear under `side-panel` and `none` in the workspace report and under no session total.
patterns.name: Four places compute a session total

patterns.description: The planner's spawn helper calls stage_of(&purpose) once, so the stage is part of the SpawnRequest. The runner copies req.stage into both ExecutionStarted (log) and NewExecution (table). The fold stores it in ExecRecord.stage. The one override is a consult spawn (Rule H3, plan.rs:516-528), which keeps the stage of the run that asked (rec.stage), although stage_of would give Handoff for Consult. A resume (ExecutionResumed) keeps the stage of the original start. Several StageKind values (Intake, Track, Sufficiency, Stakes, Staging, Format, Autofix, ImplementationReview, ClosingGate, Completion, SkillApproval, and the approval stages) are never produced by stage_of, so they never appear as an execution's stage. Several purposes map to one stage (Advise and Unblock to Rescue; Consult and handoff PromptGen to Handoff; QuickAnswer and Inspect to QuickAnswer; Detect and Adopt to Detect), and stages map to lanes via StageKind::lane().
patterns.name: Stage chosen by the planner from the purpose, stored on start

snippet.code:
pub fn stage_of(purpose: &ExecPurpose) -> StageKind {
    match purpose {
        ExecPurpose::Advise { .. } | ExecPurpose::Unblock { .. } => StageKind::Rescue,
        ExecPurpose::Consult { .. } => StageKind::Handoff,
        ExecPurpose::Explore { .. } => StageKind::Explore,
        ExecPurpose::Spec { .. } => StageKind::Spec,
        ExecPurpose::FactCheck { target: FactTarget::Spec, .. } => StageKind::FactCheckSpec,
        ExecPurpose::FactCheck { target: FactTarget::Plan, .. } => StageKind::FactCheckPlan,
        ExecPurpose::Plan { .. } => StageKind::Plan,
        ExecPurpose::Implement { .. } => StageKind::Implement,
        ExecPurpose::Review { tests: false, .. } => StageKind::Review,
        ExecPurpose::Review { tests: true, .. } => StageKind::TestReview,
        ExecPurpose::Epa { .. } => StageKind::Epa,
        ExecPurpose::WriteTest { .. } => StageKind::WriteTest,
        ExecPurpose::Docs { .. } => StageKind::Documentation,
        ExecPurpose::Architecture => StageKind::Architecture,
        ExecPurpose::PromptGen { handoff_for: Some(_) } => StageKind::Handoff,
        ExecPurpose::PromptGen { handoff_for: None } => StageKind::PromptGen,
        ExecPurpose::Verify { .. } => StageKind::Verify,
        ExecPurpose::QuickAnswer | ExecPurpose::Inspect { .. } => StageKind::QuickAnswer,
        ExecPurpose::Init { mode, .. } => match mode { /* Detect|Adopt => Detect, Scout, Propose, GenerateSkill, GenerateInventory */ },
    }
}

document.problem: A session's cost is the sum of its executions' cost_usd plus an in-memory tally of judge-call cost, and it is computed in four separate places that do not all agree on what they include. Each execution carries a StageKind from the moment it starts, in the event log and in the executions table, but the only stage-grouped cost view is a workspace-wide report that spans all sessions. Nothing today groups one session's cost by stage.
document.scope: Task: how execution costs are recorded and summed into a session's cost, and how executions map to stages. Covers the write path (usage deltas, finish, event log, executions table), every place a session total is computed, the stage assignment of each execution, and the existing workspace-wide by-stage cost report with its UI. Does not design or recommend a per-session stage breakdown, and did not open provider pricing internals beyond the Usage struct.
document.title: Execution cost recording, session cost summation, and execution-to-stage mapping

submit.findings_summary: Each execution's Usage (including cost_usd) is stored as it runs in the executions table (usage JSON plus a cost_usd column) and in the final ExecutionFinished event; resumed runs start from a usage_base so the last result is already cumulative. A session's cost is computed in four places (EngineHost::emit, Inner::append, view::summary/detail/tree_session, and SessionState::spent_usd for the budget guard); the first three add an in-memory judge-cost tally that is not persisted and is lost on restart, and spent_usd counts finished executions only. Every execution gets a StageKind from stage_of(&ExecPurpose) in the planner (consult spawns keep the asker's stage), stored in ExecutionStarted, ExecRecord.stage, and executions.stage. The only stage-grouped cost view is Costs::report's workspace-wide by_stage (NULL stage becomes 'none'), shown on the Cost screen; no per-session stage cost exists, and StageCard has no cost field.

docs.task: How the completion report is written and how the session board shows cost.

areas: web (session board, mobile session, cost screen)
asks: Explain how the completion report is written.
Explain how the session board shows cost.

data_flow.step: Every state change goes through `SessionState::fold`. When no execution runs, no project init is unfinished, and no subagent question is open, the planner's `completion` rule runs (called from the flows for each category at plan.rs lines 602 to 665).

With no `completion_decision` the planner emits `Step::Judge{Completion}`. The runner's `perform_judge` builds the input with `judge_input::judge_input(&st, JudgeKind::Completion, ...)`, which calls `completion_input`: a markdown digest of request, category, track, feedback rounds, research summaries, spec, plan, phases and their outcomes, per-project closing stages, YOLO decisions, and notes. It contains no cost.

`call_judge` resolves the judge route (tier Advanced, effort Low), calls `Services::judge` up to 3 times with the schema `{report_markdown, reason}`, adds the returned `Usage.cost_usd` to the in-memory `judge_cost[session]`, validates against `CompletionOut`, and appends `DecisionMade{judge: Completion, output}`. The system prompt is `assets/judges/completion.md`.

If the judge fails after retries, `perform_judge` appends a fallback `DecisionMade` whose `report_markdown` is '# Session complete', the error, and the raw `completion_input` text, so a report still exists.

The fold sets `completion_decision = Some(id)`. On the next planning pass the planner reads `report_markdown` from the decision output, appends `created_projects_section(s)`, and emits `Step::Complete{report_markdown}`.

`Step::Complete` writes `<session_root>/ostra-completion.md` (default body '# Session complete\n' if none), for an init session checks `init_problem` and sets the project init status, derives `summary` from the first non-empty line with leading `#` stripped, and appends `SessionCompleted{report_path, summary}`.

The fold stores `completed = Some((report_path, summary))`. `Inner::append` then recomputes the session summary and writes `cost_usd` (db execution sum + judge cost), status, lane to the sessions row and broadcasts `EngineNotice::SessionUpdated`.

The browser calls the session detail endpoint, which runs `view::detail`: it reads the report file into `SessionDetail.completion`, builds `stages` (the Completion card is Done once `completed` is set), `execution_groups` with per-group cost, and `summary.cost_usd`.

Desktop board: `SessionScreen` renders the header (total cost via `formatCost(s.cost_usd)`), `LaneStepper`, and, when `d.completion` is set, a 'Completion report' Panel from `splitDecidedForYou(d.completion).body` plus a 'Decided for you' panel. `LanePanel` renders `StageRow`s whose `meta` comes from `stageMeta`, with no cost. Live updates arrive as `session_updated` (replaces `summary`, so the header cost moves) and `session_event` (throttled reload of detail).
Mobile board: `MSession` shows total cost, the report cards, `LaneCard` stage rows (no cost), and an Executions tab that renders `execGroups(d)` with a cost per agent/project group and per execution.

patterns.description: The planner asks the Completion judge once (`Step::Judge`), the judge's answer is recorded as a `DecisionMade` and folded into `completion_decision`, the planner then emits `Step::Complete` carrying the judge's markdown, and the runner writes the file and appends `SessionCompleted`. The markdown reaches the planner only through the decision output in the log, so the fold stays a pure function of the log. Any fact the report needs that is not in the log (for example judge cost, kept in a runner-side map) is not visible to `completion_input`.
patterns.name: Completion is judge, then step, then event

patterns.description: Rule O3: `created_projects_section(s)` is appended in the planner to the judge's markdown, so a fact the engine knows exactly does not depend on the model repeating it. This is the existing precedent for adding exact data (such as a cost table) to the report without asking the judge to copy numbers. The section is built from fold state, so it stays pure.
patterns.name: Engine appends deterministic report sections after the judge's prose

patterns.description: Two precedents sum `usage.cost_usd` over executions grouped by a key: `view::execution_groups` (group = agent:project, per session, from `ExecutionView`s) and `Costs::report` in ostra-store (stage, agent, executor, session; workspace-wide, from the `executions` table). `ExecutionView.stage` and `ExecRecord.stage` already give the stage key, so a per-stage sum needs no new data. Mobile `execGroups` and the Sessions tree show the per-group figure; the desktop board does not.
patterns.name: Sum execution cost by a key, oldest first

patterns.description: The sessions row's `cost_usd` is rewritten from `db.list_executions` sum + `judge_cost[session]` on every appended event and on every usage delta. `view::detail` instead sums the execution views, passes 0.0 for judge cost, and takes the larger of that and the summary figure. The `SessionSummary.cost_usd` the board header shows is therefore executions plus judge calls; the per-execution and per-group figures exclude judge calls.
patterns.name: Session cost: DB-backed sum plus in-memory judge cost, with a max() guard

patterns.description: DTOs in ostra-core carry `#[ts(export)]`; `cargo test -p ostra-core` regenerates `web/src/api/gen/`, then `cd web && npm run typecheck`. `web/src/api/mock/fixtures*.ts` build `SessionDetail`/`StageCard` values and would need the new field. Frontend changes require asking the user to run /design-sync (CLAUDE.md).
patterns.name: API type change regenerates TypeScript

document.problem: The task name ('stage cost breakdown') implies showing cost per stage and possibly putting it in the completion report. Today the completion report is prose written by the Completion judge from a text digest of session state that contains no cost figures, and the session board shows cost only as one session total (header) plus, on mobile, per execution group. Stage cards carry execution IDs but no cost. The workspace Cost screen already aggregates spend by stage from the executions table, so a stage key and a summing precedent exist, but none of it reaches the session board or the report.
document.scope: How the completion report is written (from the planner step to the file and the event) and how the session board shows cost (backend projections and web components). Investigative only. It does not cover the workspace Cost screen beyond noting that it already groups by stage, the budget gate, or any design for a per-stage cost breakdown.
document.title: Completion report and session board cost

submit.findings_summary: The completion report is produced by Planner::completion, which asks the Completion judge once. The judge sees a text digest (completion_input) with no cost data. The planner appends engine-built sections (Rule O3), and Step::Complete writes ostra-completion.md and appends SessionCompleted. The session board shows cost only as the session total (Header.tsx, from SessionSummary.cost_usd = execution sum + in-memory judge cost) and, on mobile, per execution group and per execution (execution_groups, execGroups). StageCard has no cost field and StageRow has no cost prop, but ExecRecord and ExecutionView carry stage and usage, and the workspace Cost screen already groups spend by stage from the executions table. Judge cost is held only in the runner's in-memory map, so it is absent from stage and group sums and lost on restart.
